I mean the **app’s story memory**.

Imagine the narrator is about to say:

> “The dragon found a silver key. She opened the garden gate. A tiny fox ran out.”

If the child interrupts after hearing only “The dragon found a silver key,” the app may already have saved **all three lines** as things that happened. Its next reply could mention the fox, even though the child never heard about the fox.

So my suggestion was to keep the next part of the story consistent with what was actually played aloud. It’s a detail that matters when a child interrupts the narrator mid-sentence.
